videos.t: Cricut For Cosplay: Cutting & Scoring EVA Foam
videos.desc:
Turn your multi-day builds into 1-day builds with these techniques for your cosplay and crafting projects! In less than 5 minutes you can learn how to use your Cricut Maker (and Explore Air 2) to cut & score 2 different types of high-quality EVA foam from TNT Cosplay Supply. Beverly gives you all the settings and walks you through techniques to achieve those ultra tiny and precise cuts that would take you hours to do by hand!

EVA foam is a higher quality craft foam material available at www.TNTCosplaySupply.com. Please support them and check out their AMAZING foam and other products.

*******

Topics covered: Dr. Strange, Captain Marvel, stretch fabric, top stitching, patterning, Sew Much Cosplay’s Super Structure Foam, Cosplay Culture Magazine, sewing with stretch fabric and spandex, patterning super suits, starting & project managing those complicated super suits.

videos.t: Patterning on my 1/4 Scale 3D Printed Body Form
videos.desc: I'm patterning my Nemesis cosplay on my 1/4 scale body form, using tape. Working on a smaller scale is saving me time! It's also handy to be able to pattern on my back and figure out straps and proportions this early in the patterning stages. When I have finished the first draft of this costume pattern, I'll refine it further by tracing to thin cardboard (to simulate 4mm eva foam). After a test fitting on the 3D printed form, I'll scan and enlarge it by a factor of 4. The upscaled patterns will (theoretically) fit me and will only need minor adjustments. Fingers crossed that this works the way

Removing Glue Seams from EVA Foam!
videos.desc:
I tried a new-to-me technique of physically removing the seam in my EVA foam shield, and filling it, and IT WORKED!

Steps I will be using from now on for stubborn seams:
1. Sanding overall surface
2. Remove seams
3. Polish surface with Grinding stone
4. Heat seal
5. Apply gap filla
6. Sand gap filla
7. Apply rapid fill
8. Sand rapid fill
9. Several layers of plastidip

DragonCon is swiftly approaching….. Hope this helps anyone that wants to obliterate their seams!
